routines.semantics: raw.ducrss(a,b) returns the actual unit cross position and its derivative as a new six-component state. Pinned N0067 first divides all six components of each input by its largest absolute position component (leaving zero-position states unscaled), then calls dvcrss and dvhat. A computed zero cross therefore preserves the derivative of the internally scaled cross, not necessarily the original cross. Nonzero normalization remains sensitive near collinearity. NAIF requires caller magnitudes that avoid intermediate overflow. Inputs are readonly six-element finite states in [position,derivative] order and are not mutated. State outputs are owned arrays; actual numeric outputs are not normalized or clamped.

routines.semantics: raw.dvsep(a,b) returns the actual angular-separation derivative in radians per common derivative parameter. States share observer, frame and epoch. Pinned source normalizes both states with dvhat, returns zero if their computed position cross is exactly zero, otherwise divides the negative derivative of the normalized dot by the normalized cross norm through ZZDIV. Decimal-exponent guarded underflow returns zero, detected numeric overflow propagates as SPICE(NUMERICOVERFLOW), and exact mathematical collinearity can be poorly conditioned after normalization. Inputs are readonly six-element finite states in [position,derivative] order and are not mutated. State outputs are owned arrays; actual numeric outputs are not normalized or clamped.

scenarios.observes: Observe full angular rate and its symmetric operand reversal for well-conditioned mixed states.
Observe zero positions giving computed zero cross and static nonzero positions giving zero rate, including nonzero derivatives on zero positions.
Observe exact normalized-cross zero and scalar zero for axis-aligned parallel/opposed positions. Non-axis singular normalization residuals are separately documented, not forced to this value.
Observe signed separation rates at orthogonal positions and changing orientations.
Observe actual whole-state scaling by 1e100 and 1e-100. The angular rate retains its common-scale-invariant result.

Observe unchanged positions with derivatives alone scaled by 1e100 and 1e-100. Focused live comparison independently rescales scalar rates or the final three vector entries while preserving the first three position outputs.
Observe nonzero signed rates for near-parallel and near-opposed positions with nonzero separation, retaining the actual quotient without clamping.
Observe signed 1e-308 rates returning zero under ZZDIV, signed 1e-306 rates surviving and signed 1e308 finite rates accepted. Focused live scaling distinguishes tiny finite rates from zero.
Observe actual SPICE(NUMERICOVERFLOW) at finite positive input derivative 1.5e308; it is an error, not the C fallback scalar zero.
Observe actual SPICE(NUMERICOVERFLOW) at finite negative input derivative -1.5e308, with explicit reset/recovery tests.

findings.summary: Locked oracle returns a nonzero ill-conditioned quotient for one mathematically collinear dyadic input after normalization by sqrt21, so mathematical collinearity alone cannot establish portable exact-zero output.
findings.repair: Document exact computed-cross zero and the singular conditioning limit. Use axis-aligned parallel/opposed states for exact-zero acceptance while retaining mixed and near-parallel nonzero live cases, complete scalar comparisons and all error/cutoff cases. No global tolerance, production arithmetic or eligibility change.

findings.summary: The general header wording groups underflow with signaled numeric errors, but pinned ZZDIV returns zero without signaling for sufficiently small nonzero quotients; its overflow cutoff also precedes the maximum finite double.
findings.repair: Document and observe both signed underflow-zero values, signed tiny/large finite controls and actual signed NUMERICOVERFLOW exceptions with reset/recovery. Preserve the direct result/error distinction instead of inferring behavior from the prose.

findings.summary: The WASM genuine dvsep error test initially counted only four routine buffers and omitted three existing structured-diagnostic buffers, so its allocation-count assertion failed despite correct cleanup and scientific error behavior.
findings.repair: Count seven allocations: four routine buffers plus existing short/long/trace diagnostic buffers. Retain pointer/free accounting, NUMERICOVERFLOW assertion and recovery; no production or scientific comparator change.
